items.title: Holman Bill — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I knew her slightly, because she‟d done a tour with the Kenton band, one of those Birdland tours that I was on.

ctx.x: They didn‟t give him credit here. So I better tell – get that straightened out. Did you have much interaction with Sarah during – just for those two numbers?

Not at that time. I knew her slightly, because she‟d done a tour with the Kenton band, one of those Birdland tours that I was on. So I knew her from that and just seeing her around. I‟d written a chart for her maybe a few years before this, just for her to use in her personal appearances, but we weren‟t especially tight. I remember Jimmy Rowles had a commercial to do. He hired Sarah to do it. We did it on Sunday morning, after she‟d been up in Oakland with the Raiders. She sang the Star Spangled Banner on the…
If we follow the chronology, the mid-‟60s is a period where you give up playing the tenor saxophone. Maybe you could talk about that.

items.title: Bill Holman interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 13, 1999
items.q: Peggy Lee, Buddy Rich, Sarah Vaughan, Anita O’Day. Quite a long list here.

ctx.x: Peggy Lee, Buddy Rich, Sarah Vaughan, Anita O’Day. Quite a long list here. And all this time you’re playing also, playing in the different bands?

Yeah. I stopped doing studio work in the early 60s when all the commercial people started requiring saxophone players to play flute, and since I was writing and everything I figured I didn’t really want to take time to learn to play the flute, so that kind of went down. And then in the 60s I had some surgery on my jaw and my lip, they cut some nerves and my lip lost its strength, so I just quit playing then for about 15 years until I started my band again, and then I wanted to be able to participate, so I got the…
